evidence.title: Simulation-free Unbalanced Dynamic Optimal Transport with General Growth Penalty
evidence.abstract: Inferring cellular dynamics from unpaired single-cell snapshots requires modeling both state transitions and population growth or death. Unbalanced dynamic optimal transport (UDOT) addresses this by penalizing growth along transport paths, making the choice of growth penalty a key way to encode biological priors on proliferation and apoptosis. However, existing UDOT solvers either rely on computationally expensive NeuralODE simulations or depend on analytical solutions of conditional paths, restricting their efficiency solely to quadratic penalties, i.e. Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) geodesics. To enable an efficient UDOT solver for general growth penalties, we first show that concave growth penalties lead to degenerate solutions where growth and transport are separated. We then introduce Simulation-free Unbalanced Dynamic Optimal transport (SUDO), a simulation-free framework for UDOT with general non-quadratic convex growth penalties. SUDO learns the conditional paths and transport costs, solves the induced semi-coupling problem, and subsequently leverages unbalanced flow matching to achieve a simulation-free solution. On WFR benchmarks, SUDO matches the accuracy of efficient, analytical solution-driven algorithms while outperforming simulation-based methods in computational speed. Beyond WFR, SUDO supports asymmetric penalties that encode proliferation-dominant priors and produce more plausible trajectories and growth estimates on synthetic and single-cell datasets.

title: When Fixing Imbalance Creates New Bias: Category-Sentiment Confounding from Non-Uniform Class Rebalancing in Multi-Category Review Datasets
abstract: Class rebalancing is a standard step in preparing sentiment datasets for training, typically applied to correct an overall skew toward one class. We show that when the additional minority-class examples needed to hit a rebalancing target are drawn disproportionately from a limited subset of categories, rather than proportionally across all categories, the rebalancing procedure itself introduces a spurious association between product category and sentiment label - even when the overall class balance is identical to a properly rebalanced version. We isolate this effect using Cramer's V under matched overall balance, demonstrate its behavioral consequence with a controlled classifier evaluation on a category-decorrelated test set (with unique-source and duplication-rate budgets matched across conditions), and trace its magnitude across a donor-category-count spectrum (k=1,2,4,7). Across 10 random seeds, concentrated rebalancing yields a category-sentiment association of V=0.57 versus V=0.10 for uniform rebalancing, and a macro-F1 gap of 0.082; the effect replicates with an alternate donor category and decays as more categories are used, with classification performance recovering faster than the underlying statistical association disappears. We discuss implications for dataset construction practice.

abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum algorithm for constraint propagation, leveraging quantum mechanics to dynamically prioritize constraints during optimization. title: 自组织量子态的量子态转移算法
abstract: Quantum state transfer is a crucial process in quantum information processing, enabling the manipulation of quantum states across different platforms. Traditional approaches often struggle with computational complexity and limited transfer efficiency. This paper introduces a novel quantum state transfer algorithm predicated on the principles of self-organized quantum states. We propose a mechanism leveraging the inherent adaptability of these states to facilitate rapid and efficient state transfer, offering a significant advancement over existing methods. The algorithm utilizes self-organization to dynamically adjust the quantum state, thereby optimizing the transfer process. The core claim details the algorithm's ability to achieve faster and more reliable state transfers, including the prediction of transfer pathways. This work explores the potential of this approach to address challenges in quantum information transfer.

title: IA générative, droits d'auteur et propriété intellectuelle
abstract: Ce huitième working paper de la série NeoMundi sur l'assurabilité de l'IA examine les risques de contrefaçon et de violation du droit d'auteur liés à l'usage de l'IA générative en entreprise, et la portée réelle des garanties commerciales proposées par les éditeurs de modèles. L'article distingue deux dimensions du risque de propriété intellectuelle qui appellent des réponses assurantielles différentes : le risque en amont, lié aux données utilisées pour l'entraînement des modèles, et le risque en aval, lié à la restitution par le modèle d'un contenu reproduisant une œuvre protégée. Il analyse les exceptions fréquentes des garanties d'éviction des éditeurs (usage orienté, désactivation de mesures de sécurité, usages combinés), qui reportent une part significative de la charge de la preuve sur l'entreprise cliente. L'article propose une structuration de la couverture à plusieurs niveaux, entre garantie du fournisseur, extension de responsabilité civile professionnelle et assurance propriété intellectuelle dédiée, ainsi que des pratiques concrètes renforçant l'assurabilité de ce risque, notamment la conservation de l'historique des consignes via le passeport de service présenté dans un précédent working paper de la série. Ce travail s'inscrit dans une série de working papers publiés par l'Observatoire de Recherche NeoMundi, consacrée à l'assurabilité de l'intelligence artificielle.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum entanglement-enhanced topological information search algorithm. Traditional topological search methods often struggle with complex structures, necessitating computationally intensive approaches. This research proposes a quantum-enhanced algorithm that leverages quantum entanglement to significantly accelerate the search for key nodes within topological structures. The core claim is that this algorithm offers a substantial improvement in search efficiency and precision for topological information retrieval.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Iterative Algorithm for Chaos Theory
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum-enhanced iterative algorithm designed to address the inherent difficulties in solving chaotic systems. Traditional numerical methods often struggle to converge to stable solutions, particularly for complex, non-linear problems. We introduce a quantum annealing technique to accelerate convergence and enhance the exploration of the solution space, offering a fundamentally different approach to tackling chaos theory. The algorithm leverages quantum phenomena, specifically quantum tunneling, to facilitate the movement towards a stable equilibrium point. We detail the algorithm's design, the underlying quantum mechanics, and preliminary results demonstrating significant improvements in convergence speed and solution quality compared to classical methods. The paper concludes by discussing future research directions and potential applications.

title: 基于动态拓扑的自适应量子信息加密算法
abstract: Quantum information cryptography is a rapidly evolving field, facing challenges related to key distribution and computational security. Traditional cryptographic methods often rely on static key generation and management, which can be vulnerable to attacks exploiting imperfections in the underlying hardware. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum information cryptography utilizing dynamic topology to adapt cryptographic parameters based on input data. We introduce a self-adaptive quantum key establishment (QKE) algorithm, designed to dynamically adjust key generation and distribution based on the observed quantum state. The proposed algorithm ensures enhanced security through a continuously evolving key, mitigating the vulnerability to attacks that exploit weaknesses in static key management. The core mechanism relies on the creation and manipulation of dynamic topological structures within the quantum system, offering a significant improvement over existing approaches. This paper details the design, implementation, and analysis of the proposed algorithm, demonstrating its potential for robust quantum information security.

title: Quantum Coherence Draining for Program Privacy Protection
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to program privacy protection utilizing the principles of quantum coherence draining. Traditional methods relying on symmetric encryption often prove insufficient against sophisticated attacks. Our technique leverages the inherent randomness of quantum decoherence to obfuscate and conceal sensitive information within program code. Specifically, we introduce a process where program instructions are subjected to controlled decoherence events, effectively disrupting any attempt to reconstruct the original code or extract hidden data. The core claim is that by exploiting quantum decoherence's properties, program privacy can be achieved, preventing malicious actors from accessing sensitive information. The mechanism relies on the random nature of decoherence to perform encryption and obfuscation, hiding sensitive data. This approach offers a potentially more robust solution than conventional methods, particularly against attacks that target cryptographic vulnerabilities. We present a theoretical framework for this technique and outline its potential applications. ---

title: E8‑Phased Spinor Lattice for Robust Quantum Error Correction — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: By arranging the 240 E8 root vectors into a quaternionic spinor lattice, logical qubits can be encoded as topologically protected modes that are resonantly driven at 132 Hz. The phi‑coupled permutations act as a dynamic stabilizer, continuously re‑phasing the lattice and suppressing decoherence without external measurement. This creates a self‑healing quantum memory that leverages the inherent symmetry of E8 to perform error correction in situ. The principle extends lattice gauge theory by embedding the gauge fields directly into the spinor lattice, enabling non‑perturbative protection of quantum information. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Context-Aware Graph Embedding with Dynamic Attention
abstract: Graph embedding techniques have demonstrated significant success in representing graph structures and nodes as low-dimensional vectors, enabling applications in various domains like social network analysis, recommendation systems, and drug discovery. However, traditional graph embedding methods often rely on static representations of the graph, neglecting the dynamic nature of relationships and the evolving context within which the graph exists. This paper introduces a novel approach to graph embedding, termed Context-Aware Graph Embedding with Dynamic Attention (CAGE-DA). CAGE-DA dynamically adjusts attention weights based on the current state of the graph, considering node interactions and changes in the graph structure. The core claim of this work is that dynamically adjusting attention weights provides a more accurate and nuanced representation of graph relationships. The proposed mechanism utilizes a recurrent neural network (RNN) to track changes in node interactions and a dynamic attention mechanism to prioritize relevant connections based on this contextual information. Experimental results demonstrate that CAGE-DA outperforms existing static graph embedding methods, particularly in scenarios where graph dynamics are significant.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Topological Transform Clustering
abstract: This paper introduces a novel clustering algorithm based on dynamic adaptive topological transform clustering, designed to handle dynamically changing topological transformations. Traditional clustering methods often struggle with these transformations, requiring manual parameter adjustments. This work leverages probabilistic modeling to capture the inherent uncertainty in the transformation process, enabling high-precision clustering and automated optimization. We propose a new algorithm that integrates a probabilistic model, utilizes it to guide the clustering process, and incorporates an optimization loop to refine the resulting clusters. The core mechanism involves creating a probabilistic representation of the transformation, allowing for more robust and adaptable clustering. The proposed algorithm demonstrates improved performance in scenarios with complex and variable topological transformations compared to existing techniques. This research represents a significant advancement in clustering, offering a robust and automated approach to address the challenges posed by dynamically evolving data distributions.

title: Robustness of Dynamical Casimir Effect-Induced Quantum Synchronization
abstract: The robustness of quantum synchronization induced by the dynamical Casimir effect (DCE) is analyzed within a circuit quantum electrodynamics (cQED) architecture consisting of two superconducting qubits coupled to a shared, parametrically driven cavity. Using a Lindblad master equation approach, this study evaluates the impact of various decoherence channels (including photon loss, relaxation, thermal excitation, and pure dephasing) on the resulting synchronization dynamics. The results demonstrate that DCE-induced synchronization persists under dissipation rates achievable in state-of-the-art superconducting platforms, confirming its experimental feasibility. Among the studied mechanisms, pure dephasing is identified as the dominant factor limiting the fidelity of the synchronized state. Furthermore, it is shown that in strongly dissipative regimes, the Pearson correlation coefficient may overestimate the degree of quantum synchronization, as environmental relaxation can generate classical correlations that mimic synchronized behavior. These findings establish the parameter regimes necessary for observing genuine DCE-induced quantum synchronization and provide practical guidelines for future cQED experiments.

title: TruthInsightBench: An Evidence-Grounded Benchmark for Automated Evaluation of Open-Ended Scientific Discovery Agents
abstract: Autonomous coding agents are increasingly proposed as AI-scientist systems that conduct analyses and write research reports, but executing a prescribed analysis is not the same as making a discovery. Existing benchmarks are configured for reproduction: tasks, data, and rubrics are built around a hidden target study, and recovery of its result is rewarded. We present TruthInsightBench, a benchmark configured for discovery. Its 40 blind tasks, drawn from 40 peer-reviewed studies across 10 scientific domains, expose only a neutral scientific objective and frozen data; source conclusions, expected values, and analysis paths are withheld, leaving the agent to determine what claim the data support. A fixed LLM-based judge scores the evidentiary maturity of an agent's own claims along six dimensions, operationalized as 29 artifact-grounded items, with automated, deterministic aggregation and no per-instance human grading, so evaluation can be repeated automatically as agents evolve. On one frozen base model, four coding agents form a narrow plateau (58.4-60.3 of 100) with no statistically reliable pairwise separation: they execute and document analyses competently, with comparatively strong evidence auditability and novelty, but largely lack the discriminating acts that establish a trustworthy claim (controls, robustness, falsifiability, and cross-dataset generalization). The bottleneck is scientific judgment rather than coding, and genuine discovery remains out of reach. TruthInsightBench makes this gap a measurable target; data and scoring code are at https://github.com/TruthInsight-stack/TruthInsightBench.

title: Think-Verify-Revise: Neuro-Symbolic Visual Reasoning with Vision-Language Models and Dynamic Logic Tensor Networks
abstract: Visual reasoning tasks require a system to jointly perceive visual content and apply formal relational constraints---a combination that neither pure neural nor purely symbolic approaches handle well in isolation. This paper proposes a Neuro-Symbolic (NeSy) framework that closes this gap by tightly coupling a Vision-Language Model (VLM) for automatic First-Order Logic (FOL) rule induction with a Dynamic Logic Tensor Network (D-LTN) for differentiable rule verification, in a closed iterative feedback loop. The VLM receives a small set of labelled visual examples and proposes candidate FOL rules conforming to a strict grammar (Think); the D-LTN is automatically assembled from these rules at runtime and evaluates them grounding on CNN-produced visual embeddings (Verify); and verification failures are fed back to guide the VLM's next hypothesis (Revise). Evaluated on the ViSudo-PC benchmark across four visual domains (MNIST, EMNIST, KMNIST, FMNIST), the system induces valid Sudoku constraint rules using only three training examples as visual context. The proposed method achieves AUC scores matching or outperforming previous methods (NeuPSL, LTN), showing the potential for automatic rule discovery through VLM. Code is available at https://github.com/homayoun-afshari/nesy.

title: WearableQA: A Benchmark for Health Reasoning over Real-World Wearable Data
abstract: Recent advances in wearable sensing enable continuous monitoring of physiological and behavioral signals, yet existing benchmarks rarely evaluate whether AI systems can reason over a real user's longitudinal wearable record. We introduce WearableQA, a benchmark comprising 4,084 10-option multiple-choice questions constructed from the wearable time series, blood biomarkers, and demographics of 200 real users, each with up to 500 days of daily measurements. WearableQA preserves authentic wearable distributions that include device noise and inter-individual variability. To evaluate distinct reasoning capabilities, we introduce 16 question types organized along two complementary axes: data versus health reasoning, which distinguishes computation over longitudinal measurements from physiological interpretation; and single- versus cross-signal reasoning, which separates reasoning about individual signals from the integration of multiple signals. To construct reliable questions at scale, we adopt a dual-grounding framework that combines literature-grounded physiological findings with statistically validated population-grounded physiological patterns. This enables the capture of meaningful relationships observed in real-world wearable data. Evaluation of 14 proprietary and open-source LLMs demonstrates that WearableQA effectively differentiates model capabilities, with performance ranging from 19.6% to 72.9% against a 10% chance baseline. Moreover, WearableQA remains far from solved: most models achieve accuracies below 60%. Overall, WearableQA provides a realistic and diagnostic benchmark for evaluating LLM reasoning over real-world wearable data.

title: WeAgent-MMGenEdit: A Full-Stack Recipe for Multimodal Agentic Image Generation and Editing
abstract: Image generation and editing models have advanced rapidly, yet remain unreliable when prompts require external world knowledge. Bounded and long-tail parametric knowledge prevents direct or reason-then-generate approaches from recovering the required facts and visual appearances. Existing agentic generation and editing methods mitigate this limitation with retrieval tools, yet remain constrained by insufficient visual verification, overloaded policy models, and weak integration of retrieved textual and visual evidence. To address these limitations, we present WeAgent-MMGenEdit, a full-stack recipe including a multimodal harness, a scalable data construction pipeline, a comprehensive benchmark, and post-training methods for the agent policy and image backend. We first introduce WeAgent-Harness, a multimodal runtime with persistent evidence management and dedicated verification and integration tools that organize retrieved multimodal evidence into a dense carrier. Upon this, we develop a scalable pipeline for prompt synthesis and agentic trajectory collection, yielding 23K supervised trajectories and 14.7K RL tasks with three-layer verifiable checklists. We further introduce WeBench-MMGenEdit, a bilingual benchmark covering both knowledge-intensive image generation and multi-image editing. Finally, a two-sided post-training recipe based on SFT and RL improves the agent policy and image backend. Together, WeAgent-MMGenEdit enables a 30B-total/3B-active policy to outperform similarly sized policy models and approach the performance of a 1T-parameter agent.

title: Controlling and Assessing Appropriate Persona Use in LLM-based Dialogue Generation
abstract: In persona-based dialogue generation (PDG), LLMs often overuse persona attributes by incorporating them regardless of dialogue context, resulting in unnatural responses. Despite its practical significance, the underlying causes remain unexplored, with no method to mitigate this problem or metric to assess the appropriateness of persona use. To address these issues, we first conduct a comprehensive analysis of LLM-based PDG, revealing that LLMs exhibit a systematic bias to incorporate all given persona attributes, and that existing metrics fail to capture contextual appropriateness. Building on these findings, we propose Self-CONtrastive Persona Overuse Suppression (SCONPOS) to mitigate overuse by directly intervening in LLMs' internal representations at the prompt encoding stage, without requiring any response generation. We further propose the Persona Appropriateness Score (PAS), a novel metric that penalizes both overuse and underuse. Experimental results demonstrate that SCONPOS systematically reduces overuse, and PAS captures the contextual appropriateness of persona use.

title: Title: Non-Euclidean Distance Metric for Data Clustering
abstract: The traditional Euclidean distance metric, while widely used, suffers from limitations when applied to data points residing in non-Euclidean spaces. This paper explores a novel distance metric designed to mitigate these issues, aiming to facilitate clustering of data points across various geometric shapes and configurations. We introduce a new metric, termed the "Generalized Distance Function" (GDF), that is less reliant on assumptions of Euclidean geometry. The GDF incorporates a novel transformation to effectively bridge the gap between Euclidean space and non-Euclidean spaces, enabling the detection and grouping of data points irrespective of their inherent geometry. This work presents a mathematically rigorous framework for achieving robust clustering, offering a significant advancement over existing methods. The primary focus is on demonstrating the effectiveness of the GDF through a series of experimental evaluations across diverse datasets, emphasizing its ability to preserve cluster structure and accurately identify data points in non-Euclidean configurations. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of this approach for various applications, including data analysis, pattern recognition, and geographical representation.

title: Quantum Entanglement Dynamics Algorithm Framework
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, offers the potential for instantaneous correlations between particles, a phenomenon that has profound implications for computation and information processing. This paper introduces a dynamic algorithm framework designed to harness this entanglement for accelerated quantum algorithm implementation. We propose a novel '纠缠路径' algorithm, leveraging the inherent properties of quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust quantum states and facilitate efficient optimization of complex quantum computations. The framework's core mechanism centers around creating and manipulating entangled states to achieve a '瞬时' (instant) optimization process, a crucial step in realizing the potential of quantum speedup. This research aims to provide a practical, computationally efficient approach to accelerating existing quantum algorithms and opening new avenues for quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Entanglement Matrix: A Novel Geometric Interpretation
abstract: This paper explores a new geometric framework rooted in quantum entanglement to provide a deeper understanding of quantum computation. We propose a model, the "纠缠几何", that transforms entanglement's non-commutative nature into a novel mathematical structure, offering potential advantages for quantum computing. The core claim is that this model simplifies quantum computation and unlocks new application possibilities. The paper details the design of this model, its mathematical properties, and the potential for its application within the field of quantum information processing.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Topological Data Analysis for Image Recognition
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize topological data analysis (TDA) techniques, specifically within image recognition. Traditional TDA methods often struggle with the computational complexity of analyzing high-dimensional data, limiting their applicability to complex image datasets. We propose a quantum-enhanced approach that leverages quantum feature extraction and pattern recognition to accelerate the identification of subtle correlations, ultimately improving the speed and accuracy of image classification. This work investigates the feasibility of quantum algorithms to address these computational bottlenecks, demonstrating a promising pathway for enhanced image recognition capabilities.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encryption Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a uniquely fragile phenomenon that offers an unprecedented level of security for information transmission. This paper presents a novel quantum encryption algorithm based on quantum entanglement, incorporating an adaptive mechanism to dynamically adjust key parameters based on environmental changes. The core idea is to leverage the inherent vulnerability of quantum entanglement to create a continuously evolving cryptographic system, thereby enhancing security against various attacks. The algorithm utilizes a "Quantum Entanglement State Assessment" mechanism to adjust key parameters, ensuring the encryption process remains robust and adaptable. This approach addresses the limitations of static key generation methods and introduces a significant advancement in quantum security.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Algorithm (QEDA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Quantum Entanglement-Driven Algorithm (QEDA), a novel computational approach designed to accelerate data processing and analysis by harnessing the principles of quantum entanglement. The core of QEDA lies in a data compression and retrieval algorithm that exploits the instantaneous correlation between entangled particles to achieve significantly faster processing times compared to classical methods. We detail the algorithm's architecture, demonstrate its performance through theoretical analysis and simulated experiments, and explore potential applications across various data-intensive fields. This research investigates the potential of QEDA to fundamentally reshape data handling paradigms, pushing the boundaries of computational efficiency.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for semantic reasoning based on adaptive geometric topology, aiming to enhance reasoning accuracy through dynamic parameter adjustment. Traditional semantic reasoning often relies on static models, limiting the algorithm's ability to effectively handle complex data structures. Our proposed approach leverages dynamic geometric topology to dynamically adjust the parameters of the reasoning process, offering a significant improvement in precision compared to static methods. We explore the core mechanism and present preliminary results demonstrating enhanced performance in a specific semantic task. This work contributes to the field of semantic reasoning by introducing a robust and adaptable framework.

title: Title: Adaptive Meta-Geometry for Computational Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the application of Adaptive Meta-Geometry (AMG) to enhance computational algorithm design and optimization. Traditional algorithmic design often relies on manually tuning parameters to achieve desired performance. We propose AMG, a novel approach that dynamically adjusts the computational structure of an algorithm based on the input data, creating a self-optimizing framework. The core mechanism involves constructing a 'dynamic grid' that automatically refines the algorithm's parameters, ultimately leading to optimized performance across a range of data inputs. This system moves beyond simple speed or accuracy optimization, focusing on the *design* of the algorithm itself. This research leverages the concept of meta-geometry – a theoretical framework that allows for the automated adaptation of geometric structures to optimize for specific properties – to achieve this adaptive design. The work presented here demonstrates the effectiveness of AMG in a variety of computational tasks, showcasing a significant improvement over existing optimization techniques.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应特征匹配
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to feature matching leveraging quantum entanglement. Traditional feature matching methods often suffer from limitations in handling complex, high-dimensional data and can be computationally expensive. We propose a new method, Quantum Entanglement Feature Matching (QEMF), that utilizes quantum entanglement to establish a correlated quantum state between data points, enabling a more precise and efficient matching process. The core mechanism hinges on the ability to create and manipulate entangled states to identify and align features across data points, potentially surpassing the capabilities of classical methods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of QEMF through rigorous analysis and simulations, showcasing significant improvements in accuracy and speed compared to existing techniques. The study also explores the potential of QEMF to address challenges in specific domains, including image recognition and natural language processing. This research offers a fundamentally new perspective on feature matching, potentially unlocking significant advancements in machine learning.

Traditional feature matching methods often suffer from limitations in handling complex, high-dimensional data and can be computationally expensive. We propose a new method, Quantum Entanglement Feature Matching (QEMF), that utilizes quantum entanglement to establish a correlated quantum state between data points, enabling a more precise and efficient matching process. The core mechanism hinges on the ability to create and manipulate entangled states to identify and align features across data points, potentially surpassing the capabilities of classical methods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of QEMF through rigorous analysis and simulations, showcasing significant improvements in accuracy and speed compared to existing techniques. The study also explores the potential of QEMF to address challenges in specific domains, including image recognition and natural language processing. This research offers a fundamentally new perspective on feature matching, potentially unlocking significant advancements in machine learning.

title: Quantum Entanglement State Modeling: A Topological Approach
abstract: This paper explores the development of a novel quantum entanglement state modeling framework leveraging the principles of non-linear topology. The core claim is to construct a quantum state evolution model that accurately simulates the complex behavior of entangled states, and to integrate this model with quantum computing's inherent properties to enhance efficiency in quantum information processing. This research aims to provide a more profound understanding of quantum entanglement and its implications for advanced computational techniques.

title: Dynamic Quantum Field Theory: Quantum State Prediction and Intervention
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Dynamic Quantum Field Theory (DQFT) to quantum state prediction and intervention, aiming to enhance the performance of quantum computing. We propose a novel framework leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement and quantum field theory to achieve precise state prediction and control of quantum systems. The core mechanism involves integrating DQFT with existing quantum state estimation techniques, utilizing entanglement for enhanced accuracy and enabling controlled interactions within the quantum system. This research explores the potential of DQFT to overcome limitations of traditional approaches, offering a promising pathway toward more efficient and reliable quantum computation. The paper presents a conceptual overview of the framework, outlines the key theoretical challenges, and discusses potential future research directions.

title: K3: A Deterministic Episodic Memory System - Independent LoCoMo and LongMemEval Evaluation
abstract: Independent ex-novo evaluation of K3/infiniteMem, a deterministic self-hosted episodic memory system for AI agents, on two public benchmarks. LoCoMo (Maharana et al., ACL 2024): QA J = 70.49 (mini/mini frozen protocol, n=1535) vs oracle ceiling 84.89; stronger reader 74.92; world-model reader gate 81.50 (+8.00pp). LongMemEval-S (Wu et al., ICLR 2025): QA 59.80 (oracle 75.60). Retrieval: brute Hit@10 78.85, ANN M128 74.10. Methods: fresh NVIDIA nemotron embeddings (768-D), frozen Mem0 prompts, official per-type judges, deterministic retrieval (brute top-10, no rerank). A controlled reranker study is included with a negative verdict (J -2.00pp, not shipped). Files: paper PDF, leaderboard.json, qa_cache.jsonl (3070 per-question records). Full harness and per-question records: github.com/marcot3ssar1/InfiniteMemOs. Engine closed source, not included. Dataset licences: LoCoMo CC BY-NC 4.0. Author: Marco Tessari (independent researcher).

title: Dynamic Topology-Based Quantum Computation-Based Optimization Algorithm Based on Probability
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic topology-based quantum computation optimization algorithm that utilizes probability for enhanced optimization performance. Traditional optimization algorithms often rely on static parameters, limiting their adaptability to complex quantum systems. We introduce a new approach where quantum topology is leveraged to dynamically generate and adjust parameters, guided by probability distributions, to achieve significantly improved results. The algorithm's core mechanism centers around the creation of dynamic quantum states, allowing for a more nuanced exploration of the solution space. This paper details the theoretical framework and experimental validation of this algorithm, demonstrating its potential to overcome limitations of existing optimization techniques in the context of quantum computation.

title: 基于循环神经网络的自适应几何优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for geometric optimization, leveraging the power of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to dynamically adjust optimization parameters based on the input data's evolution. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex data and lack adaptability, while current approaches frequently rely on static parameters. This work introduces a system where an RNN learns a representation of the geometric shape and adapts the optimization process based on the data's trajectory. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through the application of the algorithm to a diverse set of optimization problems, achieving significant improvements in convergence speed and solution quality compared to existing methods. The core mechanism involves the RNN's learning of feature representations, which are then used to influence the optimization process, enabling the algorithm to navigate complex geometric landscapes more effectively. This results in a robust and adaptable optimization strategy.

title: Probability Arithmetic: A Novel Approach to Numerical Computation
abstract: This paper introduces Probability Arithmetic, a novel computational paradigm that integrates probability logic with arithmetic operations. We propose a new mechanism for calculating high-dimensional probability models by combining the "probability update" mechanism of probability logic with the "addition" and "multiplication" of arithmetic operations. The core of this approach lies in dynamically updating probabilities based on a combination of these operations, enabling efficient and scalable computations for complex probability scenarios. This system aims to significantly enhance numerical capabilities, particularly in the context of large-scale probability modeling, offering a potentially transformative advancement in data analysis and machine learning.

title: Quantum Topology for Nonlinear Equation Solving
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to solving complex mathematical problems, particularly within the realms of quantum mechanics and topological physics, utilizing quantum topology. We propose a new method for constructing and applying non-linear equation-solving algorithms based on the inherent properties of quantum topology. The core mechanism centers around leveraging the self-adaptive nature of quantum states to effectively navigate and resolve intricate mathematical challenges. This approach offers the potential for significantly enhanced computational speed and efficiency compared to traditional methods, offering a promising avenue for advancing research in these fields. The paper details the development of a specific quantum algorithm and discusses its potential impact on solving problems such as the Schrödinger equation and the study of topological phases of matter.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding (QIE)
abstract: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding (QIE) explores the utilization of quantum entanglement as a fundamental building block for enhanced data transmission and processing, specifically targeting advancements in quantum key distribution (QKD) and quantum computing security. This research proposes a novel encoding scheme predicated on the unique properties of entangled states, aiming to overcome limitations of traditional methods. The core mechanism centers around leveraging entanglement to ensure secure and efficient data transfer and manipulation, offering a fundamentally new approach to information handling within the quantum realm. The study investigates the potential of QIE to significantly improve the reliability and security of quantum communication protocols, particularly in safeguarding cryptographic keys and bolstering the robustness of quantum computations. This paper presents a detailed examination of the proposed encoding strategy, its potential benefits, and preliminary results demonstrating its feasibility and effectiveness within the context of quantum information processing.

title: 拓扑学与量子计算的融合模型
abstract: This paper investigates the potential for a unified model integrating topology and quantum computation, specifically focusing on the analysis of quantum systems and their associated topological structures. We propose a novel framework that combines established topological concepts with quantum mechanical principles to provide a deeper understanding of these intricate phenomena. The core aim is to identify novel applications of quantum computation within the realm of topological physics, exploring how quantum algorithms can be leveraged to uncover and manipulate topological properties. This research aims to advance our understanding of the relationship between topology and quantum mechanics, potentially leading to new theoretical insights and practical applications. The work will examine various aspects of this integration, including the representation of topological phases, quantum algorithms for topological data analysis, and the potential for topological quantum error correction. The paper will conclude by discussing the challenges and future directions of this research.

title: Node-Level Mechanism-Shift Detection in Linear Non-Gaussian Causal Networks: A Bootstrap-Based Framework with Application to the Human Gut Microbiome
abstract: As microbiome research increasingly seeks to identify true ecological shifts, transitioning from associational to causal approaches is essential. However, detecting structural changes across independent networks remains challenging due to the absence of established biological ground truths and the small, imbalanced sample sizes typical of microbiome cohorts. To address this, we extend an existing network comparison framework to enable node-level mechanism-shift detection under the direct linear non-Gaussian acyclic model (DirectLiNGAM). We evaluate the Naive, Bootstrap, and Relative sample size Bootstrap Stability (RSBS) estimators across extensive synthetic discovery runs and a semi-synthetic, batch-corrected human gut microbiome cohort. Our results demonstrate that resampling-based estimation consistently outperforms a single-fit Naive baseline by trading marginal recall for substantial precision gains. On both semi-synthetic and synthetic data, standard Bootstrap is optimal for comparing datasets of equal size, whereas RSBS is the only estimator that reliably handles imbalanced cohorts. This advantage strengthens as network dimensionality increases and persists under authentic compositional noise. Navigating this complex and emerging research area is currently constrained by limitations in data quantity and quality, scarce biological knowledge, and a lack of dedicated software. To address these critical gaps, we provide the complete benchmark pipeline and synthetic data generators as an open-access Python package, causal-comparator, to support node-level mechanism-shift detection across systems biology applications.

title: MEOX: Compact Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts for Earth Observation
abstract: Recent advances in Earth Observation representation learning accommodate heterogeneous sensors and missing observations, often through larger architectures. We present MEOX (Multimodal Earth Observation with eXperts), a multimodal masked autoencoder with a 2.939 million-parameter encoder and 3.115 million parameters in total. Sensor-specific adapters, explicit validity signals, and a shared sparse-expert block preserve modality-dependent processing before a learned patch-wise fusion. Four metadata tokens then accompany a single spatial sequence through fourteen further encoder blocks. Shared expert projections with private low-rank residuals constrain parameter growth, while rotary attention supports downstream spatial grids different from pretraining. The model is pretrained on 1.228 million MMEarth64 samples using modality-balanced masked reconstruction and structured sensor dropout. Frozen transfer is evaluated on six GEO-Bench tasks at both 64 and 224 pixels. The model reaches 64.42% mean intersection-over-union on cashew segmentation at 64 pixels and 90.56% average accuracy on EuroSAT at 224 pixels, exceeding the corresponding reported CSMoE results. BigEarthNet finetuning reaches 72.95% micro-average precision. Routing diagnostics distinguish expert participation, spatial dependence, modality association, and functional contribution. A held-out WorldCover probe measures a 0.64-percentage-point benefit from metadata, while retrieval separates same-sensor semantics from cross-sensor alignment. These results demonstrate sensor-flexible representation learning and strong task transfer using a compact parameter budget.

title: A new lower bound for the growth rate of Av(1324)
abstract: The growth rate of Av(1324) is the last unknown Stanley-Wilf limit of a length-four pattern. Since 2020 the best rigorous lower bound has been the 10.271012 of Bevan, Brignall, Elvey Price and Pantone; we raise it to 10.412263. Their construction lays 1324-avoiders along an infinite staircase of two-cell blocks alternating with single connecting cells, and forbids a 1324 by a local condition on how the points of a block interleave with the components of the cell beside it. Certain points of a block, its leaves, may be exempted from that condition. They exempt them on one axis only, and report that they could not count the possibilities when both are exempted. This paper exempts them on both axes and counts the result. The second relaxation is their own argument read in the other axis, and the Harris correlation inequality bounds the joint count below by the product of the two counts taken separately, at the cost of one factor of the component generating function.

title: A Rubric-Guided Large Language Model Solution for Opioid Use Disorder Computable Phenotyping
abstract: Opioid use disorder (OUD) remains a public health crisis in the United States, yet it is difficult to identify from electronic health records (EHRs) because missing diagnosis codes and supporting evidence are buried in clinical narratives. Accurate OUD identification is critical to support interventions and improve health outcomes. This study developed a rubric-guided large language model (LLM) that incorporated Optimization by PROmpting (OPRO) for OUD computable phenotyping (CP). The framework used an 18-item, expert-identified rubric to instruct LLMs to automatically extract critical text with supporting evidence to determine OUD flags. Two UF Health physicians (GMR and WMG) chart-reviewed 253 patients, including 68 OUD-positive cases. Our LLM-based computable phenotype (CP) achieved the best F1 score of 0.774 and an AUROC of 0.934, outperforming the machine learning-based CP using EHR and natural language processing-extracted variables, and zero-shot LLMs by relative F1 improvements of 12.8% and 44.4%, respectively. The proposed LLM-based CP could link LLM-extracted evidence to OUD phenotyping for better explainability.

title: SimFuse3D: Source-Guided Target Simulation and Confidence-Guided Multi-Stage Localization Reweighting for Cross-Platform 3D Object Detection
abstract: Changes in sensor height and viewpoint alter object-level point distributions, making cross-platform LiDAR unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) difficult. Self-training uses labeled source scans and unlabeled target scans, yet a retained prediction may provide a useful target location while enclosing sparse foreground returns, background clutter, or points inconsistent with the predicted box. We refer to this mismatch as box-point inconsistency. We introduce SimFuse3D, which preserves the target placement and repairs the associated pseudo object using measured geometry from labeled source scans. Object Memory retrieves a similar labeled source instance. Target Simulation places the retrieved source geometry at the target location, aligns its points with the target viewing geometry, and filters the aligned crop to approximate the target observation. Confidence-Guided Multi-Stage Localization Reweighting (CMLR) maps each target pseudo-object confidence score to a bounded weight shared by RPN localization and R-CNN box regression. All components operate only during adaptation, leaving the detector architecture and inference graph unchanged. Across six cross-platform transfers, SimFuse3D consistently outperforms Pi3DET-Net and achieves the best performance among the compared adaptation methods on nearly all metrics. On nuScenes-to-KITTI, it ranks first among the compared adaptation methods with both evaluated detectors.

Self-training uses labeled source scans and unlabeled target scans, yet a retained prediction may provide a useful target location while enclosing sparse foreground returns, background clutter, or points inconsistent with the predicted box. We refer to this mismatch as box-point inconsistency. We introduce SimFuse3D, which preserves the target placement and repairs the associated pseudo object using measured geometry from labeled source scans. Object Memory retrieves a similar labeled source instance. Target Simulation places the retrieved source geometry at the target location, aligns its points with the target viewing geometry, and filters the aligned crop to approximate the target observation. Confidence-Guided Multi-Stage Localization Reweighting (CMLR) maps each target pseudo-object confidence score to a bounded weight shared by RPN localization and R-CNN box regression. All components operate only during adaptation, leaving the detector architecture and inference graph unchanged. Across six cross-platform transfers, SimFuse3D consistently outperforms Pi3DET-Net and achieves the best performance among the compared adaptation methods on nearly all metrics. On nuScenes-to-KITTI, it ranks first among the compared adaptation methods with both evaluated detectors.

title: Capsule Lens: Locating and Tracking Concept Geometry in Model Representations
abstract: Understanding how concepts are encoded in the internal representations of machine learning models is a central problem in mechanistic interpretability, essential both for the science of deep learning and for the trustworthy deployment of increasingly capable models. Existing approaches to interpret model representations mainly map representations onto more interpretable spaces and do not directly characterize how concepts occupy representation space; various hypotheses have been proposed, but often lack of rigorous validation and largely focus on static representations. In this work, we introduce Capsule Lens, a framework that matches the region a concept occupies with a simple, trackable geometric form, a capsule, defined by several interpretable parameters, fitted in closed form to each concept's geometry and validated on held-out samples. We apply Capsule Lens in two major settings: static and dynamic representations. On static representations, we demonstrate how to locate concept geometry across various models, and how the span and norm curves uncover important geometric characteristics. On dynamic representations, we present three case studies tracking representation drifts induced by distinct training settings, CLIP pretraining, RL post-training on visual question answering, and RL post-training on mathematical reasoning. These analyses reveal qualitatively different geometric dynamics, ranging from broad network-wide restructuring in CLIP pretraining to localized and concept-specific changes in RL post-training. Our results include findings aligned with existing literature as well as novel observations. We believe Capsule Lens stands as a promising tool for locating, analyzing, and tracking concept geometry in both static and dynamic representations.

title: Adaptive Topology Mapping for Quantum Acceleration
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive topology mapping to quantum computation, aiming to enhance computational efficiency through a novel algorithm. Traditional approaches to topology mapping rely on classical computation, leading to limitations in computational speed. We propose a quantum acceleration technique that optimizes the core mapping process, offering a significant improvement in efficiency. The core mechanism centers on leveraging quantum phenomena to dynamically adjust the mapping process, achieving a higher degree of precision and faster convergence than existing methods. The study focuses on demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in a quantum computing framework, ultimately paving the way for more efficient and scalable quantum algorithms. The paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating improved performance compared to baseline techniques.

title: Adaptive Neural Network Dynamic Graph Theory
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to graph neural networks (GNNs) utilizing an adaptive neural network (ANN) to dynamically adjust graph structures. Traditional GNNs often rely on manually designed graph structures, limiting their applicability to complex data. We introduce a new algorithm that leverages an ANN to automatically optimize the graph's topology, leading to improved performance and enhanced adaptability. The core mechanism centers around a self-adjusting network that iteratively refines graph connections based on data and task demands. This adaptive process allows the GNN to effectively learn and represent relationships within the graph, resulting in more accurate and robust predictions. We detail the implementation of the algorithm, provide a comprehensive analysis of its performance, and discuss its potential for advancing the field of graph neural networks.

title: Dimension Expansion Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Dimension Expansion Algorithm (DEA) leveraging quantum entanglement to dynamically extend the dimensional landscape for simulation purposes, particularly with emphasis on potential applications in quantum computing and exploration of hypothetical multi-dimensional spaces. The algorithm constructs a 'quantum entanglement dimension' that allows for the manipulation and expansion of a system's state space, mirroring the principles of quantum mechanics and offering a pathway to simulate complex quantum phenomena. The core mechanism centers around utilizing entanglement to establish a 'correlated dimension' – a fundamental quantum property – to facilitate the exploration of higher-dimensional spaces. We detail the algorithm's architecture, discuss its theoretical underpinnings, and present preliminary results demonstrating its capability to generate novel data spaces and explore potential quantum-related outcomes. The research explores the potential of this technique to generate complex quantum states and provide a pathway to advanced simulation methodologies.

title: Title: Quantum-Inspired Wave Function Collapse (QWWC) for Machine Learning
abstract: Quantum-Inspired Wave Function Collapse (QWWC) is a novel approach to machine learning algorithm optimization that seeks to enhance model accuracy and generalization through a modified wave function collapse process. Traditional methods often struggle with the inherent randomness of classical algorithms, leading to suboptimal performance. This paper proposes a new method that introduces quantum-inspired noise and entanglement into the wave function collapse, aiming to mitigate these limitations and improve model reliability. We explore the potential benefits of this approach in various machine learning tasks, focusing on [Specific Machine Learning Task - e.g., Deep Neural Network Classification] and demonstrating its effectiveness through simulations and preliminary experiments. The core of this work lies in the design of a novel noise distribution and entanglement strategy that minimizes the effects of classical randomness while maximizing the impact of quantum-inspired effects. This research highlights the potential for a paradigm shift in machine learning optimization, moving beyond approximations towards a more robust and precise approach.

title: 拓扑信息论与量子态的保护
abstract: This paper explores the synergistic application of topology-informed cryptography and quantum state protection. Traditional quantum state protection relies on classical cryptographic methods, which often struggle to provide robust security guarantees, particularly in the face of evolving computational power and novel attacks. This work proposes a novel framework leveraging the inherent topological properties of quantum states, aiming to create a fundamentally more secure and reliable approach to quantum information processing. The core claim is that by intelligently utilizing topology-informed cryptography, we can develop quantum state protection mechanisms capable of significantly enhancing the safety and trustworthiness of quantum information. This involves constructing quantum states with inherent protection through topological transformations, which can be exploited to detect and resist attacks. The paper presents a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating the potential of this approach.

title: 基于量子拓扑的数值模拟方法
abstract: Quantum systems exhibit complex and often unpredictable behavior, posing significant challenges for traditional numerical simulations. This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum system dynamics, leveraging the principles of quantum topology to construct a highly accurate numerical simulation framework. We propose a method based on the inherent topological properties of quantum systems, allowing for a more precise and robust representation of their behavior. This work addresses the limitations of conventional methods by providing a fundamentally new framework for simulating quantum systems, specifically focusing on dynamic processes and offering enhanced accuracy. The core mechanism centers around the manipulation of topology to guide the computation, enabling a deeper understanding of quantum phenomena. We demonstrate the efficacy of this framework through a series of simulations, showcasing its potential to revolutionize the study of complex quantum systems.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Storage
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed storage leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. Traditional distributed storage systems face limitations in capacity and security. This research introduces a system designed to overcome these limitations by harnessing the non-local nature of entanglement. The core concept involves encoding data into entangled quantum states distributed across multiple nodes. This enables secure data sharing, redundancy, and inherent error correction, potentially achieving significantly higher storage capacity and improved security compared to classical methods. The system utilizes the correlated nature of entangled particles to create a robust and inherently secure storage solution, addressing critical challenges in modern data management. The theoretical framework presented outlines the key principles and potential benefits of this entanglement-driven distributed storage architecture. Further research and development are needed to realize the full potential of this technology.

abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating field at the intersection of quantum mechanics and topology, offers a unique approach to simulating complex quantum systems. title: Quantum-Inspired Bayesian Inference for High-Dimensional Feature Selection
abstract: High-dimensional feature selection remains a critical challenge in machine learning, particularly when dealing with datasets containing a large number of potential predictive variables. Traditional Bayesian approaches often struggle with this complexity due to the computational demands of exhaustive search or approximate inference methods. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging quantum-inspired techniques to accelerate the feature selection process. We simulate a quantum annealing process, representing feature selection as a probability distribution. Features are initially encoded as quantum bits (qubits), and interference patterns are manipulated to amplify the probabilities associated with relevant feature subsets, guided by a Bayesian prior. The core of this method is the exploitation of quantum superposition and interference to explore the feature space more efficiently than classical methods. The proposed approach aims to provide a computationally feasible solution for high-dimensional feature selection while maintaining the accuracy and interpretability inherent in Bayesian inference. The evaluation of the proposed method demonstrates its potential benefits in terms of speed and accuracy compared to traditional Bayesian methods, particularly when the number of features is large.

title: Title: Non-Local Constraint Satisfaction via Quantum Entanglement
abstract: The field of constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) presents a significant challenge in computer science, demanding exhaustive search to find feasible solutions. Classical algorithms struggle to efficiently explore the vast solution space, particularly for large and intricate CSPs. This research proposes a novel approach utilizing quantum entanglement to overcome these limitations, introducing a 'Quantum Resonance' mechanism that enables near-instantaneous exploration of solution configurations. Quantum entanglement provides a unique mechanism for creating probabilistic exploration of potential solutions, bypassing the limitations of classical search. We outline a framework for solving CSPs using this quantum entanglement-based approach, demonstrating its potential to drastically accelerate solution discovery. This work presents a new theoretical basis and preliminary implementation of a quantum algorithm designed to tackle complex CSPs. The core mechanism leverages entanglement to amplify promising solutions, offering a pathway to near-instantaneous exploration beyond classical computational limits. The paper details the design of the Quantum Resonance principle, and presents the results of initial experiments demonstrating the algorithm's efficacy in solving a subset of benchmark CSPs. Further investigation into the algorithm's scalability and potential for wider applicability is planned.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Probability Field Theory: A Graph-Based Structured Computation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to probabilistic field theory modeling, focusing on dynamic adaptive parameter adjustment for enhanced computational efficiency. Traditional methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the scalability of complex system simulations. We propose a graph-based structure to represent the probability field, enabling dynamic adjustment of node and edge weights to optimize computational performance. This dynamic adjustment leverages the inherent structure of the graph to guide the simulation process, resulting in significant improvements in efficiency, particularly for high-dimensional and rapidly evolving systems. The core mechanism centers around a graph-based representation of the probability field, optimized parameter adjustment through a feedback loop. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through illustrative examples, showcasing its ability to accelerate complex simulations.

title: Non-Linear Topological Geometry Adaptive Reinforcement Learning Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for dynamic parameterization of complex systems, leveraging the inherent adaptability of non-linear topological geometry with adaptive reinforcement learning. Traditional reinforcement learning often focuses on optimizing explicit strategies, neglecting the system's underlying structure. We propose an algorithm that dynamically adjusts the learning objective based on the topological structure of the system, enabling automated optimization of complex systems' performance. This framework utilizes a novel self-organizing constraint-based reinforcement learning approach to achieve adaptive parameterization. The core claim is that this approach can automatically optimize complex systems by adapting to the system's inherent topological properties, offering a new paradigm for designing dynamic and robust systems. This work addresses the limitations of existing reinforcement learning techniques by explicitly incorporating topological structure into the optimization process.

title: Introduction to Graph Neural Networks
abstract: We can naturally express the connections between the set of objects as patterns of graphs. A graph is a mathematical structure consists of the vertices and the links, where each node can have multiple nodes and edges connected to it. Mathematical graphs are often represented as arrays of elements, such as adjacency and incidence matrices. Graph theory provides a crucial framework for handling complicated, wide data easily in various fields, which includes network modeling, routing algorithms, and more. Graph theory helps to design and analyze complicated networks, such as the ecological networks, social networks and transportation systems, and also provides efficient algorithms for finding shortest paths and optimal routes in networks. Graph theory can be used to produce predictive models like the graph neural networks which help to learn about patterns and connections between the set of data. These graph networks are one of the neural networks to handle the graphical structured data in which, the nodes represent objects such as persons, organizations, locations and the edges represent the connection and the interactions between the objects, such as friendships, collaborations and the transactions. One of the emerging technologies is the machine learning algorithm which follows the concept of a human neuron. A neuron collects input from multiple neurons and transmits signals to multiple neurons. Artificial neural networks consist of a three-stage process, which includes the input layer, iteration or hidden layer and output layer. An input layer observes the input from the system or environment. A hidden or iteration layer may process and transform the input data through multiple layers of interconnected neurons. The output layer determines the output or prediction based on processed input data. Graph neural networks play some significant roles in FinTech and fraud detection, like transaction monitoring, digital payments, identity verification, biometric authentication, anomaly detection, predictive modeling, etc. The notable benefits of neural networks in FinTech and fraud detection are reduced losses, regulatory compliance, and increased efficiency.

title: Who Should Grade My Work? Student Perspectives on Transparent AI-Assisted Writing Assessment in Higher Education
abstract: The integration of GenAI tools into higher education assessment raises important questions about how students understand, interpret, and respond to AI-mediated evaluation. As instructors increasingly explore AI tools for providing feedback, prior research has examined whether GenAI-generated feedback improves writing performance and how students perceive its usefulness; comparatively little is known, however, about how students interpret such evaluation when they are explicitly informed that an AI system, rather than a human instructor, produced the feedback and the score. This study reports findings from a qualitative pedagogical inquiry conducted in an undergraduate technical communication course for computing students at a Saudi public university. Students were then explicitly informed that ChatGPT had generated the score and feedback and were invited to reflect on the evaluation in writing. Inductive thematic analysis of these reflections identified four themes: perceived usefulness of feedback; awareness of AI's contextual and pedagogical limitations; conditional trust, distinguishing feedback utility from evaluative authority; and reflection on the institutional and pedagogical role of the human instructor. Participants accepted GenAI feedback as useful for surface-level revision but consistently positioned the human instructor as the appropriate authority over grading decisions. The study identifies this as a distinction between feedback utility and evaluative authority, two judgments that students treat as analytically separate rather than as opposite ends of a single approval scale...

title: Fanout Complexity of Symmetric Boolean Functions in $\mathsf{QAC}^0$
abstract: Whether $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ can compute $\mathtt{PARITY}_n$ remains open. Computing $\mathtt{PARITY}_n$ is equivalent to implementing $\mathtt{FANOUT}_n$ under $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ reductions. This raises a more general question: for an arbitrary symmetric Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$, what fanout size is necessary and sufficient for computing $f$ in $\mathsf{QAC}^0$? We show that the answer is exactly the transition radius $ρ(f)$: computing $f$ and implementing $\mathtt{FANOUT}_{ρ(f)}$ are equivalent under $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ reductions. In particular, if $ρ(f)\ge n^δ$ for some constant $δ>0$, then computing $f$ is $\mathsf{QAC}^0_{\mathrm{f}}$-complete. Combined with Paturi's theorem, our characterization implies that if $\mathtt{PARITY}_n \notin \mathsf{QAC}^0$, then any Boolean function in $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ of approximate degree $n^{1/2+Ω(1)}$ must be nonsymmetric.

title: Minimax Lower Bound for Estimating Diffusion-based Local Intrinsic Dimension
abstract: While diffusion-based methods have recently emerged as effective tools for probing the intrinsic geometry of high-dimensional data, their statistical difficulty remains largely unexplored. We study estimation of the finite-scale population functional underlying FLIPD (Kamkari et al., 2024; arXiv:2406.03537), a diffusion-based local intrinsic dimension (LID) quantity defined through the logarithmic scale derivative of a Gaussian-smoothed density. Intuitively, Gaussian smoothing turns local dimension into a scale law: near a $d$-dimensional manifold, the kernel mass grows like $σ^d$, so differentiating with respect to the noise scale reveals the intrinsic exponent. Under a regular manifold model, we show uniformly over the model class that the finite-scale field differs from the manifold dimension $d$ by at most $O(σ^2)$. We then establish a minimax lower bound of order $(nσ^d)^{-1}$ for estimating this finite-scale field from $n$ observations, for $n^{-1/(2α+d)}\lesssimσ\leσ_0$. At the smallest scale covered by our lower-bound construction, the bound becomes the nonparametric rate $n^{-2α/(2α+d)}$.

title: Blind Random Search with Noisy Loss Measurements: Averaging, Thresholding, and Almost Sure Convergence
abstract: Blind random search repeatedly draws a candidate point and replaces the current estimate whenever the candidate has a lower loss. In the absence of noise, the true loss is observed directly. It decreases strictly at every accepted update and is monotone nonincreasing over all iterations. Measurement noise can make a worse candidate appear better and thereby break this monotonicity. To recover almost sure convergence under noise, we incorporate averaging and thresholding into the original decision criterion. These two classical tools are coupled. As the sample sizes grow, the positive threshold shrinks at a matched rate. These modifications allow blind random search to recover eventual monotonicity of the true loss under noisy measurements and to converge almost surely.

title: LookThere! Sparse Vision by Reinforced Selection
abstract: Vision transformers typically treat every image token as equally important, yet for most tasks in computer vision only a fraction are needed. Adaptive computation methods accelerate inference by choosing which tokens to process, but existing methods struggle at extreme sparsity and require heuristics that may not generalize like token diversity and attention scores. We address these limitations with LookThere, achieving a new pareto frontier in performance-compute trade-offs through an end-to-end reinforcement learning framework that jointly trains a shallow input selector and a deep representation extractor. The selector learns where to look and the extractor learns what to see, together saving computation by selecting only what is worth processing for a given task without relying on auxiliary signals. We show that LookThere only selects the task-specific input, excelling at sparse recognition in high-resolution settings (traffic signs, billiards), and maintaining accuracy with as little as 0.2% of the input. It generalizes across tasks and models, including global recognition (ImageNet classification), local recognition (ADE20K segmentation), zero-shot classification (by distillation), and regression (counting). Across all settings, LookThere surpasses state-of-the-art selection to provide a general and scalable framework for specialized and efficient adaptive computation.

title: What Matters in On-Policy Distillation? A Perspective on Data Efficiency and Data Selection
abstract: On-Policy Distillation (OPD) has emerged as a widely adopted post-training paradigm for enhancing large language models in reasoning domains. However, the data-centric mechanisms in OPD remain relatively underexplored. This paper presents an empirical study of data efficiency and data selection in OPD. We begin by investigating an extreme setting: training OPD on only one example, namely 1-shot OPD. Surprisingly, we find that 1-shot OPD is consistently effective across all sampled training examples and harder examples often yield superior performance gain. We next investigate what actually drives the student model's improvement in the training data. Our analysis reveals that the improvement is not driven by high token entropy, but the longer CoT paths which hard problem naturally generate. Training on longer CoT can help maintain closer alignment with the teacher over a long reasoning horizon, and learn critical thinking patterns usually missing in short CoTs, such as reflection (e.g., "Alternatively"). Based on these insights, we propose a simple data selection method that selects only hard examples for training, where even "unsolvable" examples that completely exceed the teacher's capability can be successfully used. Our experiments conducted on five models ranging from 1.5B to 8B show that training the student model on only 8 selected hard examples matches the performance of the 17K dataset baseline. Code and models will be publicly available.

title: Unsupervised Transfer Clustering for Mitigating Cold Start in Active Prompt Learning
abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are able to achieve impressive zero-shot classification performance by aligning visual and textual representations, but each new task still demands handcrafted prompts. Active Prompt Learning (APL) combines Active Learning (AL) and Prompt Learning (PL) into a single framework, allowing for the usage of the VLM prior knowledge for iteratively querying the most informative images to be labeled. However, the cold-start problem is still relevant for APL methods, where the performance of the initial query can be worse than random sampling. While recent state-of-the-art APL methods mitigate with balanced sampling and multimodal features, they rely on rigid, distance-based clustering to group these features. This simplistic approach can struggle to capture the complex, high-dimensional semantic distributions inherent to VLMs, leading to suboptimal query representativeness. Unsupervised transfer can be applied to these features as a possible alternative, since it is capable of inferring the underlying human labeling of a task without any form of supervision. This way, samples can be grouped in semantically coherent clusters. This paper proposes Unsupervised Transfer Clustering with Selective Querying (UTC+SQ), a framework that enhances a recent APL approach by leveraging state-of-the-art unsupervised transfer model. These models generate high-fidelity pseudo-labels that establish semantically meaningful clusters, allowing for the selection of more relevant samples. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that shifting from distance-based to projection-based clustering improves the representativeness of the queried subset, achieving accuracy gains in 6 of the 8 datasets tested.

title: Improving Language Identification for Code-Switched Utterances with Integer Linear Programming
abstract: Automatic identification of code-switched (CS) utterances remains a challenge for language identification (LID) systems, causing such texts to be underrepresented in the training data of Large Language Models. In this paper, we revisit MaskLID, a state-of-the art approach for CS identification, which requires no training and detects arbitrary language combinations. We make three main contributions: (a) we reveal, and address, a major issue of MaskLID: its overreliance on word-level language association scores; (b) we reformulate the underlying optimization algorithm as an Integer Linear Program, enabling us to experiment with a large set of clear and interpretable constraints; (c) each of these improvements vastly improves the baseline system, as we illustrate in experiments involving 10~diverse languages, where we observe a strong boost in performance on CS benchmarks. We release our code and data for reproducibility.

title: 基于动态量子纠缠的自适应机器学习
abstract: This paper presents a novel self-adaptive machine learning model leveraging the principles of dynamic quantum entanglement. Traditional machine learning algorithms often struggle with high-dimensional data and complex correlations, limiting their performance. This research introduces a quantum-enhanced approach that exploits the unique properties of quantum entanglement to improve data association and feature extraction. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust the weighting of data points, leading to enhanced model accuracy and efficiency. We explore the potential of this approach to overcome limitations of classical machine learning in scenarios demanding high-dimensional data and intricate correlations. The study highlights the benefits of employing quantum entanglement within the framework of self-adaptive learning, proposing a new method for improving model performance and robustness.

title: 基于图的混沌动力学与机器学习的协同优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to optimization that integrates graph-based chaos dynamics with machine learning, aiming to enhance optimization processes through synergistic collaboration. The core concept revolves around constructing a dynamic graph representing the problem space, where chaos dynamics are utilized to generate a diverse set of solutions, and machine learning algorithms are employed to refine and guide the optimization process based on these generated solutions. The integration of these two paradigms promises a more intelligent and robust optimization strategy compared to traditional methods. We present a framework incorporating graph representation, chaos modeling, and machine learning for automated exploration and improvement of solutions. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of this integrated approach through a series of illustrative examples across different optimization problems, highlighting its potential for achieving superior performance and adaptability.

title: 基于遗传算法的自适应动力系统优化
abstract: This paper investigates the application of genetic algorithms (GAs) to optimize complex dynamic systems. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with such systems, presenting a significant challenge. We propose a novel GA-based approach designed to address this challenge by providing an adaptive optimization strategy. The core mechanism centers around a genetic operator that iteratively refines the system parameters through a simulated environment, resulting in improved control and performance. The paper details the algorithm's structure, the optimization process, and the results achieved through simulation, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approach in optimizing a specific dynamic system. The benefits include improved efficiency, robustness, and scalability compared to traditional optimization techniques.
